text_en: In 2019 the Law on Electronic Governance and Electronic Services was adopted.
summary: The Law on Electronic Governance and Electronic Services was adopted in 2019.

text_en: Special attention is given to digitalising registers for service delivery, and to increasing the number of e-services and One Stop Shop centres, for better quality and availability of services for citizens and businesses.
summary: Priority is given to digitalising registers and increasing e-services and One Stop Shop centres.

text_en: Among others, the Programme provides measures to extend the range of digital services on the National e-Services Portal, which will reduce the administrative and financial burden for citizens and businesses and increase their efficiency.
summary: The Economic Reform Programme provides for more digital services on the national e-services portal.

text_en: Following the digitalisation of state bodies' work, the Agency implemented two electronic portals for requesters and holders of information, to be promoted in the next period as a tool for electronic submission of and response to requests for free access to public information.
summary: The Agency for free access to information implemented two e-portals for filing and answering requests.
note: RI-TEC-003 test: access-to-information portals outside the national portal; fit not fully clear.

text_en: On the other hand, although many steps were taken to establish the technical framework and ICT infrastructure (interoperability, National e-Services Portal, population register and so on), there is still a need to make better use of the potential of these solutions.
summary: Despite steps on interoperability, the portal and the population register, their potential needs better use.

text_en: The Ministry of Local Self-Government, with UNDP support, prepared analyses on the situation and potential for digitalising municipalities, with recommended implementation models, on the need and possibility of unifying e-services at local level, and on using the National Portal for services provided by local self-government units.
summary: The local self-government ministry, with UNDP, prepared analyses on digitalising municipalities and unifying local e-services.

text_en: As part of the activities of the PAR Strategy (2018-2022), in 2019 the Law on the Central Population Register, the Law on Electronic Management and Electronic Services and the Law on Electronic Documents, Electronic Identification and Trust Services were adopted; they are aligned with European legislation on digitalisation and form the legal framework for efficient and effective electronic service delivery.
summary: Three digital laws of 2019 are stated to be aligned with EU legislation and form the e-service legal framework.

text_en: Administrative barriers in special procedural laws not aligned with the Law on General Administrative Procedure are still an obstacle to digitalising processes and consistently applying that Law, and to monitoring back-office work and administrative procedures.
summary: Unaligned special procedural laws remain an obstacle to digitalising processes.
note: RI-TEC-003 test: alignment of other laws with the digitalisation package; definition does not clearly cover this.

text_en: On the other hand, although there is an e-services portal put into use in 2019 and upgraded in 2022 to deliver services to legal entities as well, the number of services does not make a significant change for businesses and citizens.
summary: The e-services portal, launched 2019 and upgraded 2022, has too few services to change much for users.

text_en: In 2019 there were 50 services, and in 2022 there are 66 services.
summary: Portal services: 50 in 2019 and 66 in 2022.

text_en: The level of the existing 95 e-services available on the National e-Services Portal is the fourth level of sophistication.
summary: The 95 e-services on the national portal are at the fourth level of sophistication.

text_en: However, delivering e-services requires greater interoperability between institutions and process automation.
summary: Delivering e-services requires greater interoperability between institutions and automation of processes.

text_en: As regards full digital inclusion, the National Strategy on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2023-2030, in preparation, provides activities to establish digital accessibility, with particular attention to the WCAG standard on all websites of public and general interest to citizens.
summary: A disability rights strategy in preparation provides for digital accessibility and WCAG on public-interest websites.

text_en: In addition, there is progressive growth in citizens' use of electronic booking of appointments at the One Stop Shop centre through the "Moj Red" platform, part of the "Zemi Brojche" system, and over 1,000 citizens have used this option in the last half of 2022 alone, since the system has been at full capacity.
summary: Over 1,000 citizens used e-booking for One Stop Shop visits in the last half of 2022.
note: Theme doubt resolved: materiality met, an online tool the public uses directly. RI-TEC-003 test: online booking for a physical service, not a transactional e-se

text_en: In addition, competences for managing some key registers in the state need centralising, to ensure a comprehensive approach to accelerated digitalisation of processes linked to these registers, which will extend the e-services on the National e-Services Portal.
summary: Competences for key registers need centralising, to speed digitalisation and extend e-services.

text_en: EU e-government benchmark indicator: 47.4% (2022), 55% (2026), 70% (2030).
summary: EU e-government benchmark: 47.4% in 2022, target 70% by 2030.

text_en: Digital transformation and development of digital services cannot be conceived without digitalising paper registers.
summary: Digital services cannot be developed without digitalising paper registers.

text_en: Digitalisation of registers and easy monitoring of roadmap activities will increase the level of digitalisation and the number of e-services available 24/7 to users.
summary: Register digitalisation and the roadmap should increase e-services available 24/7.

text_en: Citizens without adequate digital skills will have access to services through the One Stop Shop centres.
summary: Citizens without digital skills will have access to services through One Stop Shop centres.

text_en: Digitalisation should be carried out with full inclusiveness, and this measure provides for digital assistants for communication with citizens and businesses.

summary: Existing e-services on separate portals will be integrated into the national portal.

text_en: Digitalisation of the private sector is also advancing, but the competitiveness of domestic businesses could be improved through a richer offer of public e-services.

text_en: On the other hand, the capacity to access digital services and digital literacy should be significantly enhanced.
summary: The capacity to access digital services and digital literacy should be significantly enhanced.

text_en: Overall, there is a particular need to increase access to broadband, expand e-government services and develop digital skills. This should also be considered with regard to further implementation of the digital agenda for the Western Balkans and the Regional Roaming Agreement, as initiatives that could unleash the human and business potential of the country.
summary: Broadband access, e-government services and digital skills need expanding, also in view of the Western Balkans digital agenda and roaming agreement.

text_en: In line with EC recommendations, the authorities should fully implement the Law on General Administrative Procedures by completing the digitalization of institutions' registers and data exchanges and simplifying electronic procedures.
summary: In line with Commission recommendations, the authorities should complete digitalisation of registers and data exchanges and simplify electronic procedures.

text_en: The National e-portal (uslugi.gov.mk) should be improved to offer more complex e -services for citizens and businesses.
summary: The National e-portal should be improved to offer more complex e-services for citizens and businesses.

text_en: Currently, it provides services like enrolment in primary education, statements with employment and pension data, certificates of non -conviction, population register statement, various social security certificates, labour and employment data, recognition of diplomas, and many others.
summary: The National e-portal currently provides services including education enrolment, employment and pension statements, social security certificates and diploma recognition.

text_en: Setting-up of the e-Portal has been integrated into the previous Economic Reform Programmes (ERPs), and its further development could be considered as a matter of continuous efforts, i.e., the reform interventions should get a more cross - sectoral approach.
summary: Further e-Portal development is a continuous effort, and reform interventions should take a more cross-sectoral approach.

text_en: The abovementioned efforts will be supplemented by modern ICT solutions for human resources, documents management and public service delivery and further developments of interoperability among public bodies.

summary: Reform 2.2.2.3 widens public e-services on the governmental e-platform and simplifies administrative and electronic procedures.

summary: Digitally available information on compulsory charges helps lower the fiscal and administrative burden and raises private sector efficiency and productivity.

summary: Private-sector employers could use e-Rabota to advertise vacancies, register and deregister employment, and apply for active measures where the call allows.
